note.explanation: Lipids do not dissolve in water, but they dissolve in some organic solvents. Many lipids are made from glycerol and fatty acids. Fats usually contain saturated fatty acids and are solid at room temperature; oils contain unsaturated fatty acids and are liquid at room temperature. For example, animal fats are usually solid, while olive oil is liquid.
examples: Animal fats are examples of fats containing saturated fatty acids.
Olive oil is an example of an oil containing unsaturated fatty acids.
note.simple: Think of glycerol as a small backbone. Fatty acids attach to it to make many lipids. The type of fatty acid helps determine whether a fat is solid or an oil is liquid at room temperature.
note.checkQuestion: Which type of fatty acid is found in fats that are solid at room temperature?
note.title: Lipids: fats, oils and membranes
steps: Remember that glycerol has three carbon atoms, each with a hydroxyl group.
A fatty acid has a long hydrocarbon chain and a carboxyl group (COOH) at the end.
Identify saturated fatty acids by their carbon-to-carbon single bonds; they are solid at room temperature.
Identify unsaturated fatty acids by one or more carbon-to-carbon double bonds; they are liquid at room temperature.
Remember the structures: fats and oils have one glycerol and three fatty acids; phospholipids have one glycerol, two fatty acids and a phosphate group.
note.answer: Lipids include fats, oils and phospholipids. Fats and oils contain glycerol and three fatty acids; phospholipids contain glycerol, two fatty acids and a phosphate group.

written.text: What are fatty acids? Explain their types.
written.finalAnswer: Fatty acids are long hydrocarbon chains with a carboxyl group (COOH) at the end. Saturated fatty acids have internal carbon atoms bonded with the maximum number of hydrogen atoms and have no double bonds between carbon atoms; they are solid at room temperature. Unsaturated fatty acids have one or more double bonds between carbon atoms; they are liquid at room temperature.

written.text: Describe the basic structure of fats and oils. Explain how lipids play role in energy storage.
written.finalAnswer: Fats and oils contain one glycerol and three fatty acids. Fats contain saturated fatty acids and are solid at room temperature, while oils contain unsaturated fatty acids and are liquid at room temperature. Lipids are stored as fats in adipose tissues as a long-term energy reserve. When energy is required, stored lipids are broken down to release fatty acids and glycerol, which can be used as fuel for energy.

explain.title: What are lipids?
explain.body: Lipids are organic compounds that are insoluble in water but are soluble in organic solvents (e.g., alcohol, ether, benzene). They are composed of glycerol and fatty acids.

explain.title: Glycerol and fatty acids
explain.body: Glycerol is an alcohol having 3 carbon atoms. Each carbon has a hydroxyl group. Fatty acids are long hydrocarbon chains with carboxyl group (COOH) at the end.

explain.title: Saturated fatty acids
explain.body: Saturated fatty acids have internal carbon atoms bonded with maximum number of hydrogen atoms. They do not have double bonds between carbon atoms. Saturated fatty acids are solid at room temperature.

explain.title: Unsaturated fatty acids
explain.body: Unsaturated fatty acids have one or more double bonds between carbon atoms. They are liquid at room temperature.

explain.title: Fats, oils and phospholipids
explain.body: Fats and oils contain one glycerol and three fatty acids. Fats contain saturated fatty acids and are solid at room temperature; oils contain unsaturated fatty acids and are liquid at room temperature. A phospholipid molecule consists of one glycerol, two fatty acids and a phosphate group.

explain.title: Why lipids matter
explain.body: Lipids are a long-term energy reserve, essential components of cell membranes, insulators that protect vital organs, and helpers in the absorption of vitamins A, D, E and K. Some lipids also help in the synthesis of hormones.

mistakes: Do not say that saturated fatty acids have double bonds; they do not have double bonds between carbon atoms.
Do not reverse the physical states: fats are solid and oils are liquid at room temperature.
Do not give phospholipids the same structure as fats and oils: phospholipids have two fatty acids and a phosphate group.
Do not omit the carboxyl group (COOH) when defining a fatty acid.
When explaining energy storage, do not stop at saying lipids store energy; include that they are stored in adipose tissues and can break down into fatty acids and glycerol.
